key_insight: A Distil GPT2 table-to-text approach can outperform traditional machine learning and neural networks for disease prediction when clinical datasets are small, imbalanced, and low-volume.
clinical_relevance: This suggests GPT-style models may help improve screening and risk prediction from structured clinical records while highlighting clinically meaningful features even when positive cases are scarce.
method: Structured patient data were converted into physician-style text descriptions.
GPT-4 generated paraphrases were used to enrich minority-class examples before fine-tuning Distil GPT2.
Gradient-based explainable AI was used to identify influential clinical variables.
evidence_signal: Across four public datasets, the model reported average precision 0.96, specificity 0.97, sensitivity 0.96, and F1-score 0.96, with stronger and more stable performance than comparison models.
watch_item: The approach depends on synthetic paraphrasing and public datasets, so external validation and real-world testing are needed before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
